summary: The paper completes Newton–Thorne I. For every non-CM regular algebraic cuspidal π of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) and every n, it proves that Sym^n π exists (Theorem A); consequently every non-CM elliptic curve over ℚ has entire symmetric power L-functions (Corollary B). Appendix A adds the weight-one and CM cases. The proof inducts on the number of supercuspidal primes, starting from Newton–Thorne I Theorem B, by killing ramification in the manner of Khare–Wintenberger. Two things make the induction work. First, a variant of good-dihedral primes, the 'seasoned' representations with an extra Steinberg prime (Definition 3.6), which guarantee large residual image at each supercuspidal prime. Second, a new automorphy lifting theorem for symmetric powers (Theorem 2.1). It patches the rank-2 quaternionic deformation ring R together with the pseudodeformation ring P of Sym^{n−1}, where P is regular at the automorphic point by the vanishing of adjoint Selmer groups; this replaces any control of the dual Selmer group of Sym^{n−1} and works for residually reducible Sym^{n−1}, including p = 2. The endpoints are planned in ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.3 (ML.1/ML.5 for Appendix A). The method goes to one new Part II of that roadmap, beside the two proposed for Newton–Thorne I. The GL_2 inputs are planned in the Serre-conjecture, GL_2-lifting and local deformation roadmaps. Two small misprints are recorded.

items.name: Theorem A (Theorem 3.1): symmetric powers of every non-CM regular algebraic cuspidal form
items.statement: Let π be a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) which is non-CM. Then for each integer n ≥ 1, Sym^n π exists as a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_{n+1}(𝔸_ℚ) (Theorem 3.1: for n ≥ 1, Sym^{n−1}π exists).
items.locator: §1, Theorem A, p. 117; §3, Theorem 3.1, p. 139 (proof pp. 147–148)
items.note: ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.3 plans Newton–Thorne symmetric-power automorphy as an endpoint. The proof (killing supercuspidal primes with the new automorphy lifting Theorem 2.1) is routed to the Part II below; the case with no supercuspidal prime is PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21 Theorem B.

items.name: Corollary B: analytic continuation of symmetric power L-functions of non-CM elliptic curves
items.statement: Let E/ℚ be an elliptic curve without complex multiplication. For each n ≥ 2 the completed symmetric power L-function Λ(Sym^n E, s) (as defined e.g. by Dummigan–Martin–Watkins) admits an analytic continuation to the entire complex plane.
items.note: From Theorem A and the modularity of elliptic curves over ℚ (Breuil–Conrad–Diamond–Taylor); ML.3 plans these analytic consequences.

items.name: Theorem A.1: symmetric powers of weight-one and CM forms
items.statement: Let n ≥ 1 and let π be a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) with π_∞ a holomorphic limit of discrete series, or the automorphic induction of a Hecke character of a quadratic field. Then Sym^n π exists (usually not cuspidal).
items.note: Proof: the Deligne–Serre representation has dihedral, A_4, S_4 or A_5 projective image; the dihedral and CM cases are isobaric sums of Hecke characters and automorphic inductions; A_4 needs Sym², S_4 needs Sym^m for m ≤ 3, and A_5 needs Sym^m for m ≤ 4 with the tensor products GL_2 × GL_2 → GL_4 and GL_2 × GL_3 → GL_6 (Kim 2004 Theorem 6.4), via the character tables of the binary polyhedral groups. Weight-one Deligne–Serre representations are ML.1; known symmetric-power and tensor transfers are registered in ML.5.

items.name: The setting of §2
items.statement: Let p be a prime, F a totally real field, ι : Q̄_p ≅ ℂ and n ≥ 1. π is a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(𝔸_F) of weight 2, non-CM, with r_{π,ι}|_{G_{F_v}} not ordinary (Thorne 2016 §5.1; hence potentially Barsotti–Tate) at every v | p, and such that for some a ≥ 1 with p^a > max(5, 2n − 1) there is a sandwich PSL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) ⊂ Proj r̄_{π,ι}(G_F) ⊂ PGL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) up to conjugacy (so that Taylor–Wiles primes can be chosen with Sym^{n−1}r̄(Frob) regular semisimple).

items.name: Theorem 2.1: automorphy lifting for symmetric power representations
items.statement: In the setting of §2, suppose there is another regular algebraic cuspidal π′ of GL_2(𝔸_F) such that (1) π′ has weight 2 and is non-CM; (2) r_{π′,ι}|_{G_{F_v}} is not ordinary for v | p; (3) r̄_{π′,ι} ≅ r̄_{π,ι}; (4) for each place v ∤ p, π_v is a character twist of Steinberg iff π′_v is; (5) Sym^{n−1}r_{π′,ι} is automorphic. Then Sym^{n−1}r_{π,ι} is automorphic.
items.note: A new kind of automorphy lifting theorem, tailored to functoriality: it needs no dual Selmer control for Sym^{n−1}. After soluble base change one may assume (6) [F : ℚ] even, (7) det r_{π,ι} = det r_{π′,ι} = ϵ^{−1}, (8) π, π′ unramified at p, (9) Iwahori-spherical away from p with an even number of ramified places, (10) r̄ trivial on S = S_p ∪ Σ, q_v ≡ 1 mod p and π_v, π′_v Steinberg on Σ, (11) an everywhere unramified CM quadratic K/F in which S splits; then one proves Sym^{n−1}r_{Π,ι} automorphic for Π = π_K and descends.

items.name: Kisin's local lifting rings for weight-two forms
items.statement: For v | p the smallest reduced 𝒪-torsion-free quotient R_v of the fixed-determinant (ϵ^{−1}) lifting ring R^□_v through which non-ordinary crystalline lifts with Hodge–Tate weights {0, 1} factor is a domain of dimension 4 + [F_v : ℚ_p] (Kisin, Modularity of 2-adic Barsotti–Tate representations, Corollary 2.3.13); for v ∈ Σ, the quotient for extensions of ϵ^{−1} by the trivial character is a domain of dimension 4 (Kisin, Moduli of finite flat group schemes, Corollary 2.6.7); at infinite places R^{−1,□}_{V_F} (Kisin 2009 Proposition 2.5.6) is a domain of dimension 3; R^{loc} = ⊗̂R_v is an 𝒪-flat domain of dimension 1 + 3[F : ℚ] + 3|S| (Kisin 2009 Lemma 3.4.12).
items.note: Barsotti–Tate components are R08.4, Steinberg conditions away from p R08.2; the real-place and dyadic modifications are in GL2ModularityLifting R22.6.

items.name: The global deformation rings R_Q, R_Q^□ and their p = 2 variants
items.statement: For Q finite and disjoint from S: Def_Q (lifts r̃ of r̄ unramified outside S ∪ Q with det r̃ = ϵ^{−1} and local components in the R_v), represented by R_Q (R = R_∅), the framed version Def^□_Q represented by R^□_Q with R^{loc} → R^□_Q, and (for p = 2) Def′_Q, Def′^{□}_Q with the determinant condition only on S, represented by R′_Q, R′^{□}_Q.
items.note: Representability and universal representations are R04.2, local conditions and presentations R04.3.

items.name: The pseudodeformation ring P of the symmetric power determinant
items.statement: With t = det Sym^{n−1}(r|_{G_K}) and t′ = det Sym^{n−1}(r′|_{G_K}) (group determinants in Chenevier's sense) and t̄ their common reduction, P ∈ 𝒞_𝒪 is the quotient R_S of R^{[0,n−1]}_{t̄,S} of Newton–Thorne 2020 §2.19: it represents conjugate self-dual group determinants of G_{K,S} lifting t̄ with similitude character ϵ^{1−n} which are semistable with Hodge–Tate weights in [0, n − 1].
items.note: Imported from Newton–Thorne, Adjoint Selmer groups of automorphic Galois representations of unitary type.

items.name: Lemma 2.2: symmetric powers of Barsotti–Tate lifts are semistable in the torsion sense
items.statement: Let A ∈ 𝒞_𝒪 be Artinian, v ∈ S_p and r̃ : G_{F_v} → GL_2(A) a lift of r̄ of determinant ϵ^{−1} through R_v. Then A^n, via Sym^{n−1}r̃, is isomorphic as ℤ_p[G_{F_v}]-module to a subquotient of a lattice in a crystalline representation with Hodge–Tate weights in [0, n − 1]. Consequently Sym^{n−1} of the universal deformation defines a morphism P → R.
items.note: Proof: the dual of A² is the generic fibre of a finite flat group scheme; Berthelot–Breen–Messing Théorème 3.1.1 gives a crystalline lattice with weights in [0, 1] of which it is a quotient.

items.name: Taylor–Wiles data for symmetric powers and the rings P_Q
items.statement: A Taylor–Wiles datum of level N is (Q, Q̃, (α_v, β_v)_{v∈Q}) with Q places split in K, q_v ≡ 1 mod p^N, v = ṽṽ^c fixed, and α_v, β_v eigenvalues of r̄(Frob_v) such that α_v^{n−1}, α_v^{n−2}β_v, …, β_v^{n−1} are distinct. R_Q → R gives R_Q ⊗_{𝒪[Δ_Q]} 𝒪 ≅ R, Δ_Q = ∏k(v)^×(p). P_Q is the quotient of R_{S∪Q} (Newton–Thorne 2020 §2.19) of pseudodeformations t̃ abelian at each ṽ (so t̃|_{G_{K_ṽ}} is the determinant of unique characters χ_{v,1} ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ χ_{v,n} lifting ur_{α^{n−i}β^{i−1}}; Allen–Newton–Thorne Proposition 2.5) with χ_{v,i}|_I = χ_{v,m}^{n+1−2i}|_I (n = 2m) or χ_{v,m}^{(n+1−2i)/2}|_I (n = 2m + 1); the χ_{v,m} make P_Q an 𝒪[Δ_Q]-algebra and there is a universal P_Q → R_Q (𝒪[Δ_Q]-linear when n is even).
items.note: The distinctness condition is stronger than for two-dimensional lifting and is what the sandwich hypothesis makes possible.

items.name: Proposition 2.3: quaternionic Hecke modules with Taylor–Wiles level
items.statement: Let D be the definite quaternion algebra ramified exactly at ∞ and Σ, H_D(U) the 𝒪-valued functions on D^×\(D ⊗ 𝔸^∞)^×/(𝔸^∞)^×U, U_0 and U_1(Q; N) ⊂ U_0(Q) (Iwahori at Q with quotient Δ_Q/(p^N)), and m_D (with T^{(1)}_v ∈ m_D and T^{(2)}_v − 1 ∈ m_D at p), m_{D,Q}. For a Taylor–Wiles datum of level N + m_D: (1) m_D, m_{D,Q} are in the supports of H_D(U_0), H_D(U_0(Q)); (2) H_D(U_1(Q; N))_{m_{D,Q}} is free over 𝒪[Δ_Q/(p^N)] with coinvariants H_D(U_0)_{m_D}; (3) it is an R_Q-module with tr r_Q^{univ}(Frob_v) = T^{(1)}_v, det = q_vT^{(2)}_v, compatibly with the Δ_Q-actions.
items.note: Khare–Wintenberger II Corollary 7.5 and Lemma 9.1, Kisin Lemma 3.2.7, Jacquet–Langlands (GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.3). Auxiliary levels and freeness are GL2ModularityLifting R22.2.

items.name: Definite unitary Hecke modules with twisted Taylor–Wiles level
items.statement: For the definite unitary group G over F split by K (Newton–Thorne 2020 §4.1): H_G(V) = functions G(F)\G(𝔸^∞_F)/V → 𝒪; V_0 (Iwahori at Σ); for a Taylor–Wiles datum V_1(Q; N)_v = ι_ṽ^{−1}{(a_ij) ∈ Iw_ṽ : ∏_i a_ii^{n+1−2i} ↦ 1 ∈ k(ṽ)^×(p)/(p^N)} (n even) or with exponents (n + 1 − 2i)/2 (n odd), so V_0(Q)/V_1(Q; N) ≅ Δ_Q/(p^N); Hecke operators ι^{−1}T^{(i)}_w and ι^{−1}U^{(i)}_{ϖ_ṽ}; m_G (characteristic polynomial of Sym^{n−1}r̄(Frob_w) = Σ(−1)^i q_w^{i(i−1)/2}T^{(i)}_wX^{n−i}) and m_{G,Q} (U^{(i)} − q^{i(1−i)/2}∏_{j≤i}α^{n−j}β^{j−1}); twisting by characters θ of U_1 through det.

items.name: Lemma 2.4: quadratic twists on the unitary side for p = 2
items.statement: Let n be even and p = 2, and χ : F^×\(𝔸^∞_F)^×/det U_1(Q; N) → 𝒪^× quadratic. There is a unique character θ_χ of U_1(F)\U_1(𝔸^∞_F)/det V_1(Q; N) with θ_χ(z/z^c) = χ(zz^c) for all z ∈ (𝔸^∞_K)^×.
items.note: Hilbert 90 for 0 → 𝔾_m → Res_{K/F}𝔾_m → U_1 → 0.

items.name: Proposition 2.5: unitary Hecke modules with Taylor–Wiles level
items.statement: For a Taylor–Wiles datum of level N + m_G: (1) m_G, m_{G,Q} are in the supports of H_G(V_0), H_G(V_0(Q)); (2) H_G(V_1(Q; N))_{m_{G,Q}} is free over 𝒪[Δ_Q/(p^N)] with coinvariants H_G(V_0)_{m_G}; (3) it is a P_Q-module on which Λ^{univ}_i(Frob_w) (the coefficients of the universal characteristic polynomial, Chenevier §1.10) acts as q_w^{i(i−1)/2}T^{(i)}_w, compatibly with the Δ_Q-actions.
items.note: Proof: Labesse Théorème 5.4 and the existence of Π′_n (as in Newton–Thorne 2020 §4.3); via Δ′_Q, V′_1(Q; N) and P′_Q with the free action (Khare–Wintenberger II Lemma 7.4, Böckle–Harris–Khare–Thorne Lemma 8.18), Newton–Thorne 2020 Proposition 3.1 and Lemma 4.7, and Allen–Newton–Thorne Proposition 2.5 (uniqueness of the decomposition of multiplicity-free pseudocharacters).

items.name: Proposition 2.6: patched rings and modules (p > 2)
items.statement: There is q ≥ 0 such that, with W_∞ = 𝒪[[Y_1, …, Y_q, Z_1, …, Z_{4|S∪S_∞|−1}]], there are complete Noetherian local W_∞-algebras P_∞, R_∞ with P_∞ ⊗ 𝒪 ≅ P and R_∞ ⊗ 𝒪 ≅ R, a surjection R^{loc}[[X_1, …, X_g]] → R_∞ with g = q + |S ∪ S_∞| − 1, a P_∞-module H_{G,∞} and an R_∞-module H_{D,∞}, both finite free over W_∞ and specialising to H_G = H_G(V_0)_{m_G} and H_D = H_D(U_0)_{m_D}, and a morphism P_∞ → R_∞ compatible with P → R.
items.note: Proof: Taylor–Wiles data from Lemma 2.7, the framing ring 𝒯, Newton–Thorne 2020 Lemma 2.16 (P_N a quotient of 𝒪[[X_1, …, X_{g_0}]]) and the diagonalisation of Kisin 2009 Proposition 3.3.1.

items.name: The support argument: regularity of P_∞ transfers automorphy
items.statement: Given Proposition 2.6 (or 2.8), H_{G,∞} and H_{D,∞} are Cohen–Macaulay with every component of support of dimension q + 4|S ∪ S_∞| (Stacks 0BUS), so R^{loc}[[X]] → R_∞ is an isomorphism, R_∞ is a domain and H_{D,∞} is faithful; since P_(p′) = E at the point p′ of t′ (vanishing of the adjoint Bloch–Kato Selmer group of r_{Π′_n,ι}), P_∞ is regular of dimension q + 4|S ∪ S_∞| − 1 at p′_∞, so a unique component of Spec P_∞ through p′_∞ lies in Supp H_{G,∞}; the irreducible Spec R_∞ maps into it, hence p (the point of t) is in Supp_P H_G, which gives a RACSDC Π_n with r_{Π_n,ι} ≅ Sym^{n−1}(r|_{G_K}) (Labesse Corollaire 5.3), and descent (BLGHT11 Lemma 1.5).
items.note: The key new idea: a priori regularity of the pseudodeformation ring replaces killing the dual Selmer group of Sym^{n−1}.

items.name: Vanishing of adjoint Selmer groups: regularity of P at t′ (Newton–Thorne 2020)
items.statement: P_(p′) equals its residue field E, where p′ is the kernel of P → 𝒪 given by t′ (Newton–Thorne 2020 Theorem A, Proposition 2.21, Example 2.34: the adjoint Bloch–Kato Selmer group of r_{Π′_n,ι} vanishes).
items.note: Imported from Newton–Thorne, J. Eur. Math. Soc. 25 (2023).

items.name: Lemma 2.7: enough Taylor–Wiles data (p > 2)
items.statement: Let q = dim_k H¹(F_S/F, ad⁰r̄(1)) and g = q + |S ∪ S_∞| − 1. For every N ≥ 1 there is a Taylor–Wiles datum of level N with a surjection R^{loc}[[X_1, …, X_g]] → R^□_Q of R^{loc}-algebras.
items.note: As Darmon–Diamond–Taylor Theorem 2.49 (Kisin Proposition 3.2.5, Thorne 2016 Proposition 5.10), using H¹(PSL_2(𝔽_{p^a}), ad⁰) = 0 (Cline–Parshall–Scott Table 4.5) and σ with (α/β)^i ≠ 1 for i < n.

items.name: Taylor–Wiles–Kisin patching
items.statement: The abstract patching construction: from compatible systems of finite-level rings and modules with bounded cardinalities, pass by the pigeonhole principle to a subsequence and inverse limits R_∞, P_∞, H_{D,∞}, H_{G,∞} (Kisin 2009 Proposition 3.3.1).
items.note: Patching modules are DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.5 and their arithmetic application GL2ModularityLifting R22.3.

items.name: Proposition 2.8: patched rings and modules (p = 2)
items.statement: There is q ≥ |S ∪ S_∞| − 2 such that, with W_∞ as before and γ = 2 − |S ∪ S_∞| + q, there are data (1)–(4) as in Proposition 2.6 but with R^{loc}[[X_1, …, X_g]] → R′_∞ → R_∞ (g = 2q + 1), (5) a free action of Ĝ_m^γ on Sp_{R′_∞} and an equivariant δ : Sp_{R′_∞} → Ĝ_m^γ (Ĝ_m^γ acting on itself by the square of the identity), with (6) δ^{−1}(1) = Sp_{R_∞} and the action of Ĝ_m^γ[2](𝒪) on R_∞ lifting to H_{D,∞}, and (7) an action of Ĝ_m^γ[2] on Sp_{P_∞} making Sp_{R_∞} → Sp_{P_∞} equivariant and lifting to H_{G,∞}.
items.note: The 2-adic patching of Khare–Wintenberger II §2 and Kisin; deduction via the invariant ring R^{inv}_∞ (KW II Proposition 2.5) and the transitivity of Ĝ_m^γ[2](𝒪) on components of Spec R_∞.

items.name: Lemma 2.9: enough Taylor–Wiles data (p = 2)
items.statement: Let q = dim_k H¹(F_S/F, ad r̄) − 2 and g = 2q + 1. Then q ≥ |S ∪ S_∞| − 2 and for every N ≥ 1 there is a Taylor–Wiles datum of level N with |Q| = q, a surjection R^{loc}[[X_1, …, X_g]] → R′^{□}_Q, and Θ_Q/(2^N) ≅ (ℤ/2^N)^γ, γ = 2 − |S ∪ S_∞| + q, for Θ_Q the Galois group of the maximal abelian pro-2 extension of F unramified outside Q and (S ∪ S_∞)-split.
items.note: Khare–Wintenberger II Lemma 5.10 with the stronger distinctness condition.

items.name: Definition 3.2: the semisimple conductor, and sc(π)
items.statement: For π regular algebraic cuspidal on GL_2(𝔸_ℚ), sc(π) is the set of primes p with π_p supercuspidal and M_π = ∏_l N((rec_{ℚ_l}π_l)^{ss}) is its semisimple conductor.

items.name: Lemma 3.3: conductors of reducible or dihedral residual representations
items.statement: If p is odd and r̄_{π,ι} is reducible or dihedral (induced from an index-two subgroup of G_ℚ), the prime-to-p part of its conductor divides M_π.

items.name: Lemma 3.4: a non-ordinary weight-two congruence with controlled type at p
items.statement: If Proj r̄_{π,ι}(G_ℚ) contains a conjugate of PSL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) with p^a > 5, there is π′ regular algebraic cuspidal with (1) r̄_{π′,ι} ≅ r̄_{π,ι}; (2) π′ of weight 2 and not ι-ordinary; (3) rec π′_p ≅ ω_1 ⊕ ω_2 with ω_i of conductor dividing p³; (4) for l ≠ p, π_l is a Steinberg twist (resp. supercuspidal) iff π′_l is.
items.note: Proof: types M_l for the supercuspidal components (Breuil–Mézard Definition A.1.4.1), a quaternion algebra ramified at the Steinberg primes, a neat level from an auxiliary l_0, Buzzard–Diamond–Jarvis Corollary 2.12, and a dimension count on the slope-(0, 1) part of H^δ(Y(U_0(p³)), M(χ_1 ⊗ χ_2)^∨) via Hida theory and Mackey's formula (Ind^{U_0(p)}_{U_0(p³)} contains χ_1ψ ⊗ χ_2ψ^{−1} with multiplicity p + 2 or p + 1); Geraghty Lemma 5.2 for non-ordinarity.

items.name: Lemma 3.5: adding a strong local connection away from p
items.statement: If p ≥ 3 and Proj r̄_{π,ι}(G_ℚ) ⊇ PSL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) with p^a > 5, there is π′ with (1) r̄_{π′,ι} ≅ r̄_{π,ι}; (2) weight 2, not ι-ordinary; (3) rec π′_p ≅ ω_1 ⊕ ω_2 of conductors dividing p³ (so N(π′_p) | p⁶); (4) r_{π,ι}|_{G_{ℚ_l}} ∼ r_{π′,ι}|_{G_{ℚ_l}} for every l ≠ p, in particular N(π_l) = N(π′_l).
items.note: Lemma 3.4 with Gee's lifts of prescribed type (Gee 2011 Corollary 3.1.7) and BLGGT14 §1.3 ('strongly connect', Remark (6) on p. 524).

items.name: Definition 3.6: seasoned automorphic representations
items.statement: Let π be regular algebraic cuspidal of weight 2 with 2 ∉ sc(π), and q, t, r primes. π is seasoned with respect to (q, t, r) if (1) t | q + 1, t ∉ sc(π), t > max(10, 8n(n − 1)) and (q + 1)/t > 2; (2) rec π_q ≅ Ind^{W_{ℚ_q}}_{W_{ℚ_{q²}}}χ with χ|_{I_{ℚ_q}} of order t (so q ∈ sc(π), N(π_q) = q²); (3) r is a primitive root mod q and r ≡ 1 mod M, M the lcm of the prime-to-q part of M_π and ∏_{p∈sc(π)−{q}}p⁶; (4) π_r is an unramified twist of Steinberg; (5) for each p ∈ sc(π) and each irreducible dihedral ρ : G_ℚ → GL_2(𝔽̄_p) of prime-to-p conductor dividing Mq², there is a prime s with π_s an unramified Steinberg twist, ρ(Frob_s) scalar and s ≢ 1 mod p.
items.note: A variant of Khare–Wintenberger's good-dihedral condition, with an extra Steinberg prime r guaranteeing large image.

items.name: Proposition 3.7: seasoned representations have large residual image at supercuspidal primes
items.statement: If π is seasoned with respect to (q, t, r), then for each p ∈ sc(π) there is ι : Q̄_p ≅ ℂ with r̄_{π,ι}(G_ℚ) containing a conjugate of SL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) for some p^a > 2n − 1.
items.note: Proof: for p = q, irreducibility from the Steinberg prime r and Gee 2011 Theorem 4.6.1 (niveau-2 description), non-dihedrality from (5) and Lemma 3.3, and a choice of ι making the projective image contain an element of order ≥ t/2 > 4n(n − 1); for p ≠ q, inertia at q has projective order t; then the classification of finite subgroups of PGL_2(𝔽̄_p).

items.name: Lemma 3.8: the Galois group of a compositum is a fibre product
items.statement: For a finite Galois extension E/K with Galois subextensions K_1, K_2, the natural map Gal(K_1K_2/K) → Gal(K_1/K) ×_{Gal(K_1∩K_2/K)} Gal(K_2/K) is an isomorphism.
items.note: Mathlib's IntermediateField.restrictNormalHomSupProd is the injective joint restriction map; Tau Ceti identifies its range with the fibre product (IntermediateField.mem_range_restrictNormalHomSupProd_iff, TauCeti/FieldTheory/Galois/FiberProduct.lean).

items.name: Proposition 3.9: making a representation seasoned
items.statement: Let π be regular algebraic cuspidal of weight 2, non-CM, with 2, 3 ∉ sc(π). There is π′ regular algebraic cuspidal with (1) primes (q, t, r) such that π′ is seasoned with respect to (q, t, r) and sc(π′) = sc(π) ∪ {q}; (2) Sym^{n−1}π′ exists iff Sym^{n−1}π does.
items.note: Proof: t > max(10, 8n(n − 1), N(π)) with t ≡ 1 mod 4 and large t-adic image, q ≡ −1 mod t with Frob_q conjugate to complex conjugation, r and the primes s_{i,j} by Chebotarev with Lemma 3.8, then Gee 2011 Corollary 3.1.7 and BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1 (Fontaine–Laffaille at t; Sym^m of SL_2(𝔽_t) irreducible for t > m).

items.name: Proposition 3.10: removing one supercuspidal prime
items.statement: Let π be regular algebraic cuspidal of weight 2, seasoned with respect to (q, t, r), and p ∈ sc(π) with p ≥ 5. There is π′ of weight 2, non-CM, with sc(π′) = sc(π) − {p}, still seasoned with respect to (q, t, r) if p ≠ q, such that Sym^{n−1}π′ existing implies Sym^{n−1}π exists.
items.note: Proposition 3.7 chooses ι, Lemma 3.5 produces π′ and Theorem 2.1 transfers automorphy.

items.name: Proposition 3.11: the weight-two case with 2, 3 ∉ sc(π)
items.statement: If π is regular algebraic cuspidal of weight 2, non-CM, with 2, 3 ∉ sc(π), then Sym^{n−1}π exists.
items.note: Induction: (H_k) ⇒ (H′_{k+1}) by Proposition 3.10 and (H′_k) ⇒ (H_k) by Propositions 3.9–3.10; (H_0) is Newton–Thorne I.

items.name: The reductions in the proof of Theorem 3.1
items.statement: For π of weight 2 with 2 ∉ sc(π) and π_3 supercuspidal: choose t > max(5, 4n(n − 1), N(π)), t ≡ 1 mod 4, with large t-adic image, and q ≡ −1 mod t, q ≡ 1 mod 8, q ≡ 1 mod every prime l < t, Frob_q conjugate to complex conjugation; a good-dihedral π′ at q (Gee 2011 Corollary 3.1.7) with Sym^{n−1} equivalent to that of π (BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1); the 3-adic image of π′ contains PSL_2(𝔽_{3^a}) with 3^a > 2n − 1 (Khare–Wintenberger I Lemma 6.3); Lemma 3.4 gives π″ with 2, 3 ∉ sc(π″), Proposition 3.11 and Theorem 2.1 conclude. The case 2 ∈ sc(π) replaces 3 by 2; weight k > 2 reduces to weight 2 through a t-adic congruence (t > max(5, k(n + 1))) and BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1 with potential diagonalisability (Gee–Kisin Lemma 4.4.1).
items.note: Printed with r̄_{π,ι} where r̄_{π′,ι} is meant in the 3-adic image step (sourceIssues E1).

items.name: Good-dihedral primes and residual image control (Khare–Wintenberger)
items.statement: A form with a supercuspidal component at a good-dihedral prime q (inertia character of order t, t ≡ 1 mod 4, q ≡ 1 mod 8 and q ≡ 1 mod the primes below t) has large residual projective image at the relevant primes (Khare–Wintenberger I Lemmas 6.3 and 8.2).
items.note: Good-dihedral primes and their image control are ClassicalSerreModularity R27.1 and R33.2.

items.name: Automorphic lifts of prescribed type for GL_2 (Gee 2011)
items.statement: Gee 2011 Corollary 3.1.7 (with Proposition 3.1.5): given a modular r̄ with suitably large image, there is a weight-2 regular algebraic cuspidal π′ with r̄_{π′} ≅ r̄ with prescribed local behaviour — unramified Steinberg twists at chosen primes, a supercuspidal type at q, and r_{π,ι}|_{G_{ℚ_l}} ∼ r_{π′,ι}|_{G_{ℚ_l}} elsewhere; Theorem 4.6.1 describes r̄|_{I_{ℚ_q}} for such types.
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R24.3 plans the prescribed local lifts, including 'any prescribed-type strengthening from Gee/Snowden used by the modern route'.

items.name: Types for supercuspidal Bernstein components of GL_2(ℚ_l) (Henniart's appendix to Breuil–Mézard)
items.statement: For π_l supercuspidal there is, after enlarging E, an 𝒪[GL_2(ℤ_l)]-module M_l, finite free over 𝒪, with M_l ⊗ ℂ a type for the Bernstein component of π_l (Breuil–Mézard Definition A.1.4.1); and for principal-series types χ_1 ⊗ χ_2 on U_0(p^r), rec π′_p ≅ ω_1 ⊕ ω_2 with ω_i ∘ Art|_{ℤ_p^×} = ιχ_i and Hom_{U_0(p³)}(χ_1 ⊗ χ_2, π′_p) one-dimensional (A.2.4).
items.note: Types for GL_2 belong with the types Part II proposed by PAPER-FINTZEN-21.

items.name: Automorphy lifting for residually irreducible symmetric powers (BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1)
items.statement: If Sym^{n−1}r̄ is irreducible (e.g. its image contains SL_2(𝔽_t) with t > n − 1), Sym^{n−1}r is potentially diagonalisable at t (Fontaine–Laffaille, or Gee–Kisin Lemma 4.4.1 with the remark after BLGG11 Definition 3.3.5) and Sym^{n−1}r′ is automorphic with r̄ ≅ r̄′, then Sym^{n−1}r is automorphic.
items.locator: §3, proofs of Proposition 3.9 and Theorem 3.1, pp. 145–148
items.note: The residually irreducible polarized lifting theorem is in the Part II proposed by PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25.

items.name: Quaternionic automorphic forms of given type and the Jacquet–Langlands correspondence
items.statement: For a quaternion algebra D over ℚ ramified at the Steinberg primes Σ (and at ∞ iff |Σ| is odd), the cohomology H^δ(Y(U), M(χ_1 ⊗ χ_2)^∨) of the locally symmetric space of level U (Newton–Thorne 2016 §3.1) localised at m_π is non-zero (Buzzard–Diamond–Jarvis Corollary 2.12), and its systems of eigenvalues come, by Jacquet–Langlands, from cuspidal π′ of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) of weight 2 with prescribed Steinberg and supercuspidal types.
items.note: Global Jacquet–Langlands is GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.3; quaternionic Galois representations AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.2.
